scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports they suddenly cannot reach
pc2 (200.1.1.2) or anything else in the partner AS. pc1 can still
ping its own gateway 195.11.14.1 normally. The partner operator
reports their side is healthy internally: pc2 still reaches its
gateway 200.1.1.1 fine. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and its watchdog) on router1

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1 bgpd
Mechanism: router1 (AS 1) is pc1's only gateway and the local eBGP
  speaker toward router2 (AS 2) over the 193.10.11.0/24 inter-AS
  link. With bgpd dead on router1, the eBGP session to router2
  drops: router1 loses the learned route to 200.1.1.0/24 and stops
  advertising 195.11.14.0/24, so router2 withdraws it too. Traffic
  between pc1 and pc2 fails in both directions. Local segments are
  unaffected (pc1<->195.11.14.1 and pc2<->200.1.1.1 still work).
Localization: router1
Root cause: bgpd not running on router1
Fix: restart FRR on router1 (`service frr restart`)

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is missing/empty on router1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR/bgpd on router1 (`service frr restart`). Once bgpd is running again,
the eBGP session to router2 re-establishes, router1 re-learns and re-advertises
the inter-AS prefixes, and pc1 reaches pc2 normally. router2 needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: bgpd / BGP daemon not running
bonus-rules-out-link: notes the inter-AS link (router1 eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon failure from a link cut

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on **router1**: the `bgpd` process was killed and is no longer running, while the watchfrr supervisor is also absent, preventing any automatic restart.

**Mechanism:** At lab start (~00:50:02) router1's bgpd came up, established an eBGP session with router2 (AS 2) over the 193.10.11.0/24 interconnect, and successfully exchanged prefixes — router1 advertised 195.11.14.0/24 and received 200.1.1.0/24. At 00:51:31 the FRR log shows zebra reporting `Client 'bgp' encountered an error and is shutting down` followed by `client 27 disconnected 1 bgp routes removed from the rib`, meaning bgpd exited and zebra immediately withdrew the learned BGP route 200.1.1.0/24 from the kernel FIB. Router2's session consequently fell to the `Active` state (unable to reach TCP port 179 on router1). Both routing tables now contain only directly connected prefixes — neither router carries any BGP-learned routes.

**Localization:** Exclusively router1. Router2's BGP configuration, its bgpd process, and its local reachability are all intact. The /etc/frr/daemons file on router1 correctly specifies `bgpd=yes` and /etc/frr/frr.conf holds the correct `router bgp 1` configuration, so the configuration itself is healthy — only the running process is missing.

**Root cause:** The bgpd daemon on router1 was killed (injected fault) and watchfrr is not running to respawn it, leaving the inter-AS BGP session permanently down.

**Fix:** Restart bgpd on router1: `service frr restart` (or `systemctl restart frr`). This will reload frr.conf, relaunch bgpd, re-establish the eBGP session with router2, and restore the 200.1.1.0/24 route in router1's RIB, restoring full pc1 → pc2 reachability.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names and localizes the fault to router1 in both the summary and localization sections.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: bgpd / BGP daemon not running
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states the bgpd daemon on router1 was killed/not running and not being respawned, correctly identifying the BGP daemon as the failed component.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-link: notes the inter-AS link (router1 eth0) is UP, distinguishing a daemon failure from a link cut
per_axis.rationale: The report never explicitly states that router1's inter‑AS interface (eth0/193.10.11.0/24) is UP to rule out a link cut—only the daemon failure is described.
Recommending restarting FRR/bgpd on router1 (service frr restart or systemctl restart frr) matches the expected fix and will restore the eBGP session and routes.

The agent's log contains direct observations (bgpd not running, no watchfrr process, frr.log showing bgp client shutdown, frr.conf and daemons present) and the writeup’s inferences follow logically from those observations. The investigation covers the necessary checks to localize the fault to router1 and identify the killed bgpd/not-respawned condition as root cause.
